relevance_note: Case series of three Spanish lipid-clinic patients with familial LCAT deficiency with individual detail: "We report three FLD patients, two of them siblings", homozygous c.605T>C p.(Ile202Thr) in the siblings and c.512G>A p.(Arg171Glu) in the third.
method_note: Hand-built with a short Python script in the scratch directory; every value comes from my reading of the paper, and the script only checked spans and fields. Labels: the paper calls the patients 'First Case', 'Second Case', 'Third Case' (Table 1 column headers; Tables 2-3 rows) and in text mostly 'the first/second/third case' or 'patient'; the lowercase text form 'first case'/'second case'/'third case' is used. Figure S1 legend gives pedigree labels I.1 (first case) and I.3 (second case). Table 1 has patients as columns (headers 'First Case', 'Second Case', 'Third Case', 'Reference Values'); spans quote the row label through the patient's cell. Features derived from Table 1 numbers (hypertriglyceridemia in the second and third cases, low apo A-I, low apo B in the third case, elevated creatinine) rest on the paper's own printed reference range, quoted as the whole row; the text does not itself call these values abnormal (except TG in the first case). The second case's TG of 158 is only slightly above the printed 30-149 range. Rial-Crestelo D et al. [30] family (Discussion): included as two literature persons ('ref [30] patient' with FLD; 'sister of ref [30] patient' with FED, female) because the paper says they carry 'the same LCAT mutation'; no variant is printed, so their variant rows are 'not reported'. Other family members of the siblings were tested (Figure S1, 'all available family members') but get no individual detail in the text, so no rows. The PLS-DA individual 'later diagnosed with extreme HDL deficiency' is not described as having LCAT deficiency, so out of scope. Heterozygous p.(Ile202Thr) carriers from ref [22] are a group without individual detail, so no rows. Transcript NM_012108.3 is the reference the Methods name for LCAT sequencing; it is recorded for all three patients. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) LCAT activity: Results text gives exogenous activity '1.70 nmol/h*mL, 0.05 nmol/h*mL and 1.35 nmol/h*mL, respectively' and FER '1.40%, 1.5% and 1.9%' for cases 1-3, while Table 1 gives exogenous 0.05 / 1.7 / 1.35 and FER 1.50 / 1.40 / 1.90, i.e. the first and second cases are swapped; both are cited in functional_evidence_statement. (2) First case: Table 1 'Currently age, years 88' but the text says hemodialysis at 75 and death 12 years later (about 87); recorded age at last evaluation 88 as printed, vital status deceased, age at death left null (not stated directly). (3) Third case small HDL-P: text says 0.01 µmol/L, Table 2 gives 0.38. (4) FPLC text says both siblings had 'lower LDL-cholesterol levels' than the control, but the second case's Table 2 LDL-C (107.44 mg/dL) exceeds the control population mean (81.5) and her apo B (131) is above range; the checklist item low LDL/apo B is left 'not reported' for the siblings and no feature row was made for it. Hedged: the second case's 67% free cholesterol is said only to be 'suggesting the presence of some LpX', so lipoprotein X is 'not reported' for her. Third case: 'mild impaired renal function'/'early renal disease' were not mapped to the checklist item 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure' (left not reported); 'thickening of capillary walls' was not mapped to GBM thickening, and 'foamy lipid deposits' not to glomerular foam cells. Ethnicity/country left 'not reported': the patients attend a lipid unit in Aragon, Spain, but their origin is not stated. is_proband left null: no one is called proband or index case.
